## Goal

Reconnect with Quarto by mapping it onto the R Markdown you already know. By the end you
will have written a short `.qmd` report with headings, an inline calculation, a code chunk
that produces a figure, and a cross-referenced caption.

Throughout, remember the one-line mental model: **Quarto is R Markdown that grew up.**

---

## 1. Open or create this file

This file **is** the lab. Render it now and confirm you get an HTML page.

- In **RStudio**: click the **Render** button (or `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+K`).
- In **Positron**: open the Quarto preview / run render from the editor toolbar.

You should see a styled HTML document open in the Viewer.

## 2. Quarto vs R Markdown, in your own words

The chunk grid below is rendered statically. Experiment with the chunk options `echo`, `eval`, `message`, `warning`, `fig-cap`, and `include`.

::: {.callout-tip title="Setting chunk options in Quarto"}
In Quarto, **R** chunk options are set using the `#|` prefix inside the chunk, rather than in the curly braces `` ```{r, echo=TRUE}``` `` as in R Markdown.
:::

```{r}
plot(cars)
```

From previous R Markdown experience and experimenting with Quarto below, write a short paragraph describing the differences you notice between R Markdown and Quarto using either bullet points or enumerated lists:

*Your prose*

## 3. Inline code

The mean of the numbers 1 to 10 rendered inline is produced by <code>&#96;r mean(1:10)&#96;</code> and rendered as `r mean(1:10)`. Below, write your own inline expression that reports the number of rows in `mtcars` in the following sentence:

There are ____________ rows in `mtcars`.

## 4. A figure with a caption and cross-reference

Execute the chunk below. It draws a histogram with a caption. Take note of the chunk label
(`#| label: fig-mpg`): you reference it elsewhere with `@fig-mpg`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-mpg
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of highway mileage in mtcars"
#| fig-alt: "A histogram of the hwy column of the mpg dataset"
library(ggplot2)
ggplot2::mpg |>
  ggplot(aes(hwy)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "#2E7D6B", color = "white")
```

A sentence that points at the figure: see @fig-mpg for the distribution.

Now add a second figure (a scatter plot of `hwy` vs `cty`) below, give it a label and caption,
and cross-reference it in a sentence. Render the document and confirm both figure numbers update.

## 5. A project-level `_quarto.yml`

Quarto shines with **projects**. Create a `_quarto.yml` file next to this lab (same folder) with
a shared HTML theme, so every `.qmd` in the folder gets the same look:

```yaml
project:
  type: default
output-dir: _output

format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-title: "On this page"
    theme: cosmo
```

Render again. The output should now move into `_output/` and gain a table of contents.
